About DW
Why DW Transport Consultancy exists

Built from years of spotting the things others walk past.

I am Daniel Williams CMILT, a transport professional based in West Sussex. Since leaving the army, transport is what I have known: operations, people, compliance records, systems, reporting and the pressure of keeping work moving safely.

In previous roles I have repeatedly found savings by analysing the small things people often miss: duplicated entry, repeated reports, manual workarounds, disconnected systems, unclear ownership and jobs being done simply because that is how they have always been done.

DW exists because those little things add up. The aim is not to make people less valuable. It is to free them from low-value admin, protect the business they represent, and give operators clearer data, safer processes and better control.

If a task only exists because nobody has reviewed it, it deserves to be challenged.

Look at the operation through three lenses.

Operators do not need buzzwords. They need clearer systems, safer workforce control and data that shows where the real waste sits.

Tech that joins upTacho, dashcams, telematics, maintenance and reporting working from the same evidence.
Ops that protect peopleSafer routines, clearer escalation and workforce management that protects the business.
Data that proves itFigures, reports and records that show what happened, not what someone retyped later.
Dashcams, tacho, telematics, maintenance and admin systems.Make them speak to each other before asking people to bridge the gap manually.

Systems should reduce admin, not create another place to check.

DW reviews where data is already being created and how it could be reused across the business instead of being retyped, chased or rebuilt in spreadsheets.

  • Dashcams and telematicsUse footage, behaviour data and incident evidence to support drivers and protect the operator.
  • Tacho and driver analysisTurn exceptions, infringements and patterns into practical management actions.
  • System integrationConnect planning, maintenance, invoicing, reporting and customer updates so information moves once.
  • AI and automationAutomate repeatable admin carefully, with human checks where the risk needs them.
Safe workforce, protected business.Good processes should protect drivers, managers, customers and the licence.

Operations are about people as much as vehicles.

Processes should help managers run the workforce safely, fairly and consistently while protecting the business those people represent every day.

  • Workforce safetyReview the routines that shape driver behaviour, communication and escalation.
  • Manager visibilityMake it easier to see risk early: hours, defects, fatigue signals, repeated incidents and weak handovers.
  • Business protectionBuild evidence trails that support drivers and the company if something is challenged.
  • Practical controlKeep procedures simple enough that they are followed when the office is busy.
The savings are often in the boring bits.Repeated minutes, repeated checks and repeated work become real cost.

Fix the operating rhythm before adding more software.

Most admin waste is hiding in ordinary handovers: the job moves from order to plan to driver update to invoice evidence, but the same information gets typed, checked and chased more than once.

Where the savings usually show up.

Most operators already have the information somewhere. The issue is how often people have to chase it, rebuild it, retype it or explain why two reports disagree.

Repeated admin

One job, too many updates

Orders get entered, planned, amended, chased, recorded and invoiced across different tools. DW looks for the points where one reliable update could remove three manual ones.

Evidence gaps

Hard to prove what happened

Driver records, defects, camera evidence, vehicle activity and customer updates should support each other. Weak links cost time when there is a dispute, incident or audit question.

Disconnected systems

People become the integration

When telematics, tacho, maintenance, planning and finance do not speak, the traffic office fills the gap. That is where careful automation and cleaner reporting can pay back quickly.

Quick admin waste estimate

Put a rough cost against repeated transport admin.

This is a simple sense-check, not a finance model. Estimate the total hours your team spends repeating office tasks, then see the rough monthly and annual cost before anyone has even looked at disputes, missed evidence or delayed invoicing.

Use the total across the office, rather than a fleet-size estimate. For example, 2.4 hours means roughly 2 hours 24 minutes of repeated work each day.

What it helps you question

The checklist is not a legal sign-off. It is a way to spot where admin, records, evidence and reporting may already be showing you where time, money or control is leaking.

  • Are drivers, vehicles, defects, incidents and maintenance records easy to find when needed?
  • Are the same updates being typed into more than one place?
  • Do reports match what actually happened in the operation?
  • Could dashcam, tacho, telematics or planning data remove manual chasing?
  • Are people doing work because it adds value, or because nobody has reviewed it?

Questions operators normally ask first.

Short answers before anyone books time in the diary.

Do you work remotely or on site?

Both. Some admin, systems and reporting reviews can start remotely. Yard, workforce and operational rhythm work is usually stronger with at least some time on site.

Is this a formal compliance sign-off?

No. DW provides operational review, admin checks and practical improvement actions. Formal legal advice or statutory compliance sign-off should sit with the correct appointed professionals.

What systems can you look at?

Planning tools, spreadsheets, telematics, dashcams, tacho analysis, maintenance records, driver records, reporting packs and the handovers between them.

Do you cover outside the UK?

Yes. DW is UK based and can support operations with full EU coverage, especially where UK operators need stronger visibility across cross-border work.

What happens on the first call?

A short discussion about the issue, the systems involved, where time is being lost and whether a fixed-scope review is the right next step.

Got a spreadsheet, report or process that everyone relies on and nobody trusts?

Send a quick email with the issue: admin time, evidence gaps, reporting, systems, telematics or AI-ready process improvement. If it is not a good fit, you will get a straight answer.
